ai.description: This skink reaches 8–10 cm snout-vent length. It is brown with three distinct longitudinal yellow stripes and dark lateral bands. It features smooth, overlapping scales and a long, slender tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Eutropis trivittata* is best distinguished by the three distinct, dark longitudinal stripes on its back, which are bordered by prominent white or pale dorsolateral lines.
ai.habitat: *Eutropis trivittata* typically inhabits dry deciduous forests, scrublands, and rocky outcrops across the Indian subcontinent, often found at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Three-banded Mabuya is a diurnal lizard that actively hunts insects and small invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky terrain during the warmest parts of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eutropis trivittata* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–7 eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eutropis trivittata* is endemic to peninsular India, primarily occurring in the Western Ghats and Deccan Plateau across elevations from sea level to 1,200 meters.
